request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Small requested changes expanded into rewrites.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Compare the work with the request before responding.",
    "description": "Use for tasks.",
    "name": "scope-check"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "A skill can guide scope management."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":2,"justification":"\"Compare the work with the request before responding\" names no concrete check, threshold, or corrective step to take when a mismatch is found, so it's unlikely to change behavior reliably."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"The body is a bare platitude (\"compare the work with the request\") that offers no specific guidance distinguishing appropriate scope expansion from scope creep."},"trigger_quality":{"score":1,"justification":"The description \"Use for tasks.\" is not a real Use-when trigger — it matches virtually any task and gives no signal for when this skill should fire."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy content contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or identifiers from the evidence — it is entirely generic (if too much so)."},"routing_fitness":{"score":2,"justification":"The rationale (\"A skill can guide scope management\") doesn't justify why a full skill is needed over a cheaper always-on remedy like a feedback memory or CLAUDE.md rule for a general behavioral tendency like this."}}

actionability.justification: "Compare the work with the request before responding" names no concrete check, threshold, or corrective step to take when a mismatch is found, so it's unlikely to change behavior reliably.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The body is a bare platitude ("compare the work with the request") that offers no specific guidance distinguishing appropriate scope expansion from scope creep.

leakage.justification: The remedy content contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or identifiers from the evidence — it is entirely generic (if too much so).

routing_fitness.justification: The rationale ("A skill can guide scope management") doesn't justify why a full skill is needed over a cheaper always-on remedy like a feedback memory or CLAUDE.md rule for a general behavioral tendency like this.

trigger_quality.justification: The description "Use for tasks." is not a real Use-when trigger — it matches virtually any task and gives no signal for when this skill should fire.
